title: Turkish Airlines flight 158
summary: Turkish Airlines Flight 158 operating a Boeing 727 crashed near Ankara Esenboğa Airport on 16 January 1983 in severe winter weather. The aircraft landed approximately 50 meters short of the runway in driving snow and gusty winds, struck an obstacle, broke into three pieces, and caught fire. The crash killed 47 of the 67 occupants on board, with most fatal injuries occurring in the middle section of the aircraft that caught fire.
probable_cause: The aircraft landed short of the runway in driving snow and severe weather conditions, struck an obstacle, broke apart and caught fire.

title: Air Canada 797
summary: Air Canada Flight 797 was enroute from Dallas to Montreal when an in-flight fire developed in the rear lavatory at 18:48. The fire spread between the outer skin and inner decor panels, filling the aircraft with toxic smoke and burning through electrical cables that disabled most cockpit instrumentation. The captain exercised outstanding airmanship to divert the aircraft to Cincinnati for an emergency landing. However, 90 seconds after landing and opening the exit doors, fresh oxygen entering the cabin created a backdraft that engulfed the interior in flames, killing 23 passengers trapped in the fuselage.
probable_cause: A fire of undetermined origin in the rear lavatory. The NTSB noted the flight crew underestimated the fire's severity and the decision to land at Cincinnati was correct, but the post-landing flashover during evacuation proved unsurvivable for those unable to escape.

The aircraft had suffered an explosive decompression in 1979 that required rebuilding the tail section and replacing most wiring and hydraulic lines in the back.
Ninety seconds after landing and doors opened, the heat and fresh oxygen created a backdraft that immediately engulfed the plane's interior in flames, killing 23 passengers unable to evacuate.
The plane's interior became engulfed in flames after landing when the exit doors were opened.

title: 1983 TAME 737-200 crash
summary: Captain Terán had received only three weeks of simulator training and 30 hours of Boeing 737 flight time. During final approach to Cuenca in foggy conditions, the crew became distracted discussing labor problems and experimenting with aircraft controls. The ground proximity warning system activated but the aircraft struck Bashún Hill 1 mile from the airport.
probable_cause: Pilot error directly caused the crash. The crew was not properly trained on the Boeing 737, not fully familiar with the aircraft controls, and became distracted while trying to locate the runway in heavy fog, causing descent below minimum safe altitude.

title: Aeroflot 5463
summary: The Tu-134A collided with Dolan Mountain during descent to Almaty. Air traffic control gave an erroneous instruction to turn and the crew mistakenly chose an incorrect heading of 199 degrees instead of 140. Although ATC subsequently corrected the heading, it instructed the crew to descend to 600 m where the minimum safe altitude was 4620 m. The crew chose to descend anyway instead of climbing when they knew they were on a collision course.
probable_cause: Crew error in following an erroneous ATC instruction to descend below safe altitude; the crew continued descent to 600 m despite knowing of mountainous terrain, violating flight regulations by not immediately climbing when aware of danger.

The aircraft crashed into Dolan Mountain at an altitude of 690 m, 30 km from Almaty airport, disintegrating and catching fire

title: Korean Air Lines 007 crash
summary: Korean Air Lines Flight 007, a Boeing 747 flying from New York to Seoul via Anchorage, drifted off its planned route owing to a navigational mistake by the crew and flew through Soviet airspace on 1 September 1983. Soviet Air Forces treated the unidentified aircraft as an intruding US spy plane and destroyed it with air-to-air missiles from a Sukhoi Su-15 interceptor after firing warning shots; it crashed into the sea near Moneron Island, killing all 246 passengers and 23 crew.
probable_cause: The aircraft strayed from its assigned route owing to a navigational mistake by the crew and entered Soviet airspace, where it was treated as an intruding US spy plane and shot down by a Soviet interceptor after firing warning shots.

events.text: Flight 007 departed Gate 15 of John F. Kennedy International Airport at 00:25 EDT on August 31, 1983, 35 minutes behind schedule.
Less than a half-minute after taking off from Anchorage, air traffic control directed KAL 007 to turn to a magnetic heading of 220 degrees toward route J501.
Owing to a navigational mistake, the airliner drifted from its planned R20 airway and flew into Soviet airspace off the Kamchatka Peninsula.
The Soviet Air Forces treated the unidentified 747 as an intruding U.S. spy plane and fired warning shots before a Sukhoi Su-15 launched air-to-air missiles.
The missiles destroyed the airliner, which crashed into the sea near Moneron Island west of Sakhalin, killing all 246 passengers and 23 crew.

title: Gulf Air 771
summary: While on approach to Abu Dhabi, the Boeing 737 experienced an explosive detonation in the baggage compartment planted by the Abu Nidal Organization. Fire broke out immediately and the aircraft crashed in the desert near Jebel Ali. All 112 people on board, including 105 passengers and 7 crew members, were killed by the bombing.
probable_cause: The bomb was planted by the Abu Nidal Organization to convince the United Arab Emirates to pay protection money to Nidal so as to avoid attacks on their soil.

title: 1983 TAAG Angola Airlines 737 Boeing crash
summary: The Boeing 737 crashed just after taking off from Lubango Airport. The aircraft was at 200 ft and climbing when it began to descend and turn left. The left wingtip hit the ground, and the aircraft broke apart and burst into flames. Post-crash investigation reported no conclusive evidence of hostile action, and the cause of the crash is officially considered to be a mechanical failure.

title: Avianca 011

agencies.name: Civil Aviation Accident and Incident Investigation Commission

summary: Avianca Flight 011 crashed on a hill approximately 7.5 miles southeast of Madrid Barajas Airport during an ILS approach on November 27, 1983. The captain, a highly experienced pilot, incorrectly determined the aircraft's position during the instrument approach in night conditions with low visibility. The aircraft struck terrain on three different hills, killing 181 passengers and crew on board.
probable_cause: Pilot error in the form of an incorrect determination of the aircraft's position relative to the runway during the instrument landing system approach in night conditions and low visibility, resulting in controlled flight into terrain.

It was night at the time of the accident with visibility of 5 miles.

title: Madrid Runway Disaster
summary: An Aviaco DC-9 taxiing for takeoff on runway 01 accidentally made a wrong turn in dense fog and entered the active runway, directly into the path of an Iberia Boeing 727 beginning its takeoff roll. The 727 crew attempted to rotate for liftoff but had not achieved flying speed. The aircraft's rear fuselage struck the DC-9. Poor visibility combined with inadequate airport signage and taxiway markings prevented the DC-9 crew from recognizing they had taxied onto the runway.
probable_cause: The DC-9 crew made a wrong turn in fog due to inadequate airport signage and taxiway markings, inadvertently taxiing onto the active runway. The 727 crew's attempt to lift off at insufficient speed did not prevent collision.

title: Aeroflot 601
summary: Aeroflot Flight 601, an Antonov An-24RV, crashed near Leshukonskoye on 24 December 1983 while attempting to land. The captain descended with a significant left deviation of about 490 meters and decided to land instead of executing a go-around, then banked right to correct. At 30 meters altitude he attempted a go-around but the aircraft reached critical slip angles and stalled. After reaching 90 degrees left bank angle at 80 meters altitude, the aircraft crashed 110 meters right of the runway. Forty-four of 49 occupants were killed.
probable_cause: The investigation placed responsibility on Captain Alimov, who displayed risky piloting style that violated flight instructions. The crew should have initiated a go-around instead of attempting to land first, and the premature go-around attempt at low altitude resulted in a stall and loss of control.
